To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the expression of EGFR and HPV status are independent prognostic factors in oropharynx cancer; (2) EGFR expression in oropharyx cancer is associated with HPV status, and (3) the combination of EGFR expression and HPV status may be a useful marker to predict prognosis in oropharx cancer.
HPV status is a strong prognostic marker for oropharyngealsquamous cell carcinomawhich has been validated in several large studies.
(a) the presence of HPV in oropharynx squamous cell carcinomas is associated with a favorable prognosis, and (b) HPV-negative tumors are more likely to be EGFR positive.

a study of the role of the human papillomaviruses (HPV) in the development of oropharyngealsquamous cell carcinoma and the role of HPV in predicting response to therapy and prognosis.

the development of a new method for the analysis of a large number of data, and the use of the method in order to analyze the results of a clinical trial.
